=== task --help ===
task mutates the devboard task file rendered by the dashboard —
the in-flight detail worklog itself deliberately does not store: plan item
states, contract scorecard, decisions, code-to-know, and the needs-you
attention queue.

Target resolution: --id names the task file slug (searched across all repo
groups). Without --id, the task file whose group matches the current git
repo is used when exactly one exists. An --id that resolves to a file in a
DIFFERENT repo than the current one is refused (the file likely belongs to
an unrelated task that happens to share the slug) — pass --force to adopt
it anyway.

When --id names an epic, --child <child-id> is required — every in-flight
subcommand below then targets that child's own entry in the epic's
children list, never the epic file's (unused) top-level fields. --child is
rejected when --id names a plain ticket. An --id that is ITSELF a child of
an epic (has a Parent in WORK.md) is refused outright: pass --id <epic>
--child <that-id> instead, so a stray per-child file is never recreated.

All subcommands are silent no-ops (exit 0, notice on stderr) when the
devboard data dir does not exist. See devboard/schema.md for the file
format and field-ownership rules.

Usage:
  worklog task [command]

Available Commands:
  code        Add a code-to-know entry (a load-bearing change the human should see)
  complexity  Rate the task's complexity (throttles fan-out depth)
  decision    Record an implementation decision (or contract amendment)
  needs-you   Add or resolve attention-queue entries
  phase       Set the task's workflow phase
  plan        Add, reword, remove, or re-state a plan item (1-based index)
  scorecard   Add, reword, remove, or set the status of a scorecard criterion (1-based index)
  untrack     Stop showing this task on the dashboard (deletes only its task file)
  waiting-on  Track questions blocked on external parties (who, age, answer)

Flags:
      --child string   child ticket id (required when --id names an epic; rejected otherwise)
      --force          reuse an --id that already names a task file in a different repo
  -h, --help           help for task
      --id string      task file slug (default: the current repo's only task)
      --json           emit a JSON result object instead of styled text

98	def _parse_task(path, archived=False):

474	// idExistsInNotes scans every notes/*.md for a `- [ ]` or `- [x]` line
475	// whose first token matches id (case-insensitive). Returns the notes file
476	// path and true on the first match.
477	func idExistsInNotes(wd model.Workdir, id string) (string, bool) {
478		entries, err := os.ReadDir(wd.NotesDir())
479		if err != nil {
480			return "", false
481		}
482		re := regexp.MustCompile(`^- \[[ ~x]\]\s+([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)`)
483		target := strings.ToLower(id)
484		for _, e := range entries {
485			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
486				continue
487			}
488			path := filepath.Join(wd.NotesDir(), e.Name())
489			data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
490			if err != nil {
491				continue
492			}
493			for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
494				m := re.FindStringSubmatch(line)
495				if m == nil {
496					continue
497				}
498				if strings.EqualFold(m[1], target) {
499					return path, true
500				}
501			}
502		}
503		return "", false
504	}

2	
3	A browser dashboard over a directory of task files, so the human
4	can follow agent work without living in terminal scrollback. Agents (or
5	anyone) drop one YAML/JSON file per task into `<data-root>/<repo>/`; the
6	page renders plan todos, the contract scorecard, decisions, code-to-know,
7	a "needs you" attention queue, tier/complexity/worklog badges, and a
8	copy-`claude --resume` button per task (from the `session` field) — and
9	hot-reloads within ~2s of any file change, no refresh needed (SSE,
10	auto-reconnecting).
11	
12	Tasks with a `worklog:` join key also render the ticket's
13	`notes/<id>.md` live from the worklog data dir (second read-only mount) —
14	rendered, never copied, and note edits hot-reload too. That mount also
15	carries `FEEDBACK.md`, rendered as the global Friction panel (see below).
16	
17	The intended writer is the `worklog` CLI (`start`/`done`/`pr` side
18	effects plus the `worklog task` family, including `untrack` to stop
19	tracking a task by deleting only its YAML) — but a hand-dropped
20	schema-valid file is fully supported.

23

26	mkdir -p ~/.local/share/devboard
27	docker compose up --build -d
28	# open http://localhost:8484
29	```

## Findings

**Why Next/Someday tickets are invisible today:** The dashboard's data model *is* task files — `_all_tasks()` in `devboard/server.py` only lists `<repo>/*.{yaml,yml,json}` under `$DEVBOARD_DATA`. Task files are created exclusively by `devboard.OnStart()`, which only `worklog start` calls (`worklog/internal/cli/start.go`). `worklog add --section Next|Someday` never touches devboard at all. So a ticket sitting in `## Next`/`## Someday` in `WORK.md` simply has no file to be discovered — it's not filtered, it's structurally absent from the source the dashboard reads.

**Relevant existing plumbing:** `WORK.md` is already mounted read-only into the devboard container at `/worklog` (`compose.yaml:8`, `$WORKLOG_DATA`), and `server.py` already does lightweight parsing against that same mount for `FEEDBACK.md` and `notes/<id>.md` — so there's precedent for the server reading worklog data directly, not just task-file data. However, the devboard container is `python:3.12-alpine` with no Go toolchain and no `worklog` binary (`Dockerfile`), so shelling out to `worklog status --json` isn't available today without adding a build step to cross-compile and vendor the binary into the image.

## Recommendation

Have `server.py` parse `## Next`/`## Someday` (and probably `## Blocked`/`## Waiting`, which have the same "no task file" gap) directly out of the already-mounted `WORK.md`, and merge those as lightweight synthetic entries into the `/api/tasks` response — rendered in a distinct "Backlog" lane in `index.html`, visually and interactively separate from real task cards (no plan/scorecard/decisions, since those fields don't exist yet). Keep this path strictly read-only: `WORK.md` stays the single source of truth and only the `worklog` CLI ever mutates it.

Concretely:
- Add a small, deliberately minimal parser in `server.py` that extracts just `- [ ] **ID** — Title` + the `Type`/`Section` metadata lines — not the full `worklog/internal/parse` grammar. This limits the surface that can drift if the `WORK.md` format changes, at the cost of some duplication between the Go and Python parsers.
- Tag synthesized entries (e.g. `source: "worklog"`, `phase: "queued"`) so the frontend filter (`index.html:568`) and card renderer can distinguish them from file-backed tasks without touching the schema in `schema.md`.
- Don't create task files for Next/Someday tickets (the alternative approach) — that would blur the documented ownership model where a task file means "an agent workspace with a plan," and would add a reconciliation burden (stub files need cleanup on ticket deletion, and need to transition into a real task file when `worklog start` later fires for the same ID).

The trade-off worth flagging: this is two parsers of one format. If that duplication is unacceptable, the cleaner long-term fix is a `worklog status --json` (or similar) flag so Go remains the single parser and `server.py` just shells out to it — but that requires vendoring the compiled `worklog` binary into the Alpine image, which is a real (if small) infra change versus the read-only mount that already exists.

Want me to turn this into a plan for implementation, or leave it here as the research writeup?
